title: Pakistan Foreign Office Urges India to Comply 'in Letter and Spirit' With Hague Ruling on Indus Waters Treaty
detail: Pakistan's Foreign Office spokesperson Tahir Andrabi, addressing the ministry's weekly press briefing on September 2, 2026, said the Permanent Court of Arbitration's August 31 merits award had reaffirmed that the Indus Waters Treaty 'remained fully in force and binding' and rejected India's unilateral attempt to place it in abeyance. Andrabi said Pakistan 'welcomes the clear and authoritative pronouncements' of the ruling, remains committed to implementing the treaty 'in letter and spirit,' and 'will continue to urge India to reciprocate with the same approach' — adding that Pakistan retains all diplomatic and legal options to protect its water rights and urging New Delhi to return to full treaty compliance. The statement follows Deputy PM/Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar's September 1 remarks that the award 'decisively rejects India's unlawful attempt' to suspend the treaty, and PPP Senator Sherry Rehman's comments welcoming the ruling's limits on the Ratle hydro project. India's Ministry of External Affairs has maintained since August 31 that the Court of Arbitration has 'no jurisdiction whatsoever' over India's sovereign decisions and that the treaty remains in abeyance until Pakistan credibly ends cross-border terrorism support.

confidenceReason: On-record statement by Pakistan FO spokesperson at a formal press briefing, confirmed by Pakistan's official state news agency (APP) plus multiple Tier-2 outlets.

title: Ruling NC and Opposition BJP Stage Rival Gherao Protests in Srinagar and Jammu Over Statehood, Governance
detail: Jammu & Kashmir's ruling National Conference (NC) and opposition BJP staged simultaneous rival protests in Srinagar and Jammu on September 2, 2026. NC workers, led by party president Farooq Abdullah, gheraoed BJP's Srinagar and Jammu headquarters (the latter at Trikuta Nagar), demanding restoration of full statehood, constitutional guarantees, clearance of the reservation file and accountability for promises the Union government made in Parliament and before the Supreme Court; Abdullah said the people of J&K 'would no longer remain silent' over the denial of statehood. BJP workers separately gathered at Ghanta Ghar, Lal Chowk, and attempted to march on the Civil Secretariat, accusing the Omar Abdullah-led NC government of failing on unemployment, power cuts, water shortages, a recent electricity tariff hike and delayed Panchayati Raj elections. Jammu and Kashmir Police deployed riot personnel, sealed key routes and blocked both marches from reaching their targets, detaining activists from each side; officials said the heavy deployment was meant only to keep the rival camps apart, not impose a blanket ban on protest.
